title: Slice & Stretch Scenario Lab — decision knobs for cycle capacity
creator: Leah Gomez
description:
Objective: Build a lightweight, repeatable Slice & Stretch Scenario Lab to help PMs and EMs make defensible staffing and scope-cut decisions during cycle planning. The lab is a compact workbook + decision matrix that accepts headcount, commit velocity, critical-path services, and OKR priorities and outputs: (1) three prioritized scope slices (must-have / stretch / backlog), (2) recommended staff reassignments or surge lanes, and (3) confidence bands for delivery risk and customer impact.

Deliverables: 1) canonical Google Sheets template with formulas and sample historical baselines; 2) a short PRD describing knobs and trade-offs; 3) a triage playbook doc for senior PM/Eng leaders; 4) two worked examples (runtime-1.18 release vs. console-2026.02 minor work).
acceptance_criteria: Sheet template ingests: FTE by role, % allocation, historical cycle throughput, and key milestone dates
Sheet auto-computes three scope slices and shows estimated cycle burn (story points or ideal days)
Triage playbook covers at least three cut heuristics (customer-facing, SLO-critical, regulatory) and a final arbitration flow
Two worked examples included and validated by at least one Eng lead and one PM
Template stored in Confluence with instructions and linked to the cycle planning board

updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff with Eng leads; agreed to use story-point-equivalent baseline (velocity) and include an alternate FTE-days view for on-call and infra work.
2026-02-25: PM analytics delivered cycle throughput for last four cycles; initial volatility (±18%) observed for infra-heavy initiatives.

2026-03-03: Prototype sheet completed; validated must/should/could slices against runtime-1.18 sample. Observed that caching work compresses scope more than kernel-level perf work for the same FTE cost.

2026-03-07: Workshop #1 feedback: include an explicit knob for "operational debt" that reserves ~10% capacity for incident response; Eng requested an alternate view that estimates token-cost impact for infra work.
2026-03-10: Iterated sheet with an "emergency surge" lane option and tie-in to release-rollback signal thresholds; planning to run Workshop #2 on 2026-03-12.
decisions: Adopt three-slice output (Must / Stretch / Backlog) as canonical for cycle planning
Use story-point-equivalent velocity as primary baseline; provide FTE-days as alternate input
Default operational-debt reserve of 10% in the template unless project lead requests otherwise
Surge lanes will be represented as temporary reassignments (not hiring) and require an explicit owner and acceptance criteria
tradeoffs: Conservative slices increase predictability but may under-deliver on aspirational OKRs
Aggressive consolidation of tasks into must-have reduces backlog but raises risk of degraded reliability or missed quality gates
Surge lanes are effective short-term but increase cross-team coordination overhead and ramp cost
Modeling token-cost impact improves decision quality for infra work but needs additional data and adds complexity to the sheet
notes: Plan: After finalizing, we will run the lab as part of the 2026-W12 cycle kickoff and measure variance vs. actual delivery to calibrate the model.
Follow-up: Consider integrating the sheet into the Console as a simple planning widget (longer-term product work request).
Owner: Marco will shepherd data inputs; Leah will finalize the playbook and coordinate exec readout.
